title: SkyLink infrastructure is built by individual Prime Agents but owned by Sky Core and shared with all of them
content:
A.2.2.8 sets out an unusual ownership arrangement: "SkyLink Primitives are built autonomously by Prime Agents, but **owned by Sky Core and shared among all Prime Agents**. Prime Agents are reimbursed for the cost of setting up SkyLink Primitives and given additional first-mover incentives."

This is a direct answer to a free-rider problem. Bridge infrastructure to a new chain is expensive to build, cheap to reuse, and benefits every Agent once it exists — exactly the profile of a good that no rational individual actor funds. Rather than centralizing construction, the Atlas keeps building decentralized and socializes both the cost and the asset.

Three components make it work. **Autonomous construction** means capability grows wherever an Agent sees an opportunity, not where a central roadmap points. **Sky Core ownership** prevents the builder capturing a private toll on shared infrastructure. **Reimbursement plus first-mover incentives** restores the private return that ownership would otherwise have provided.

The trade-off is a coordination gap. Because Agents build autonomously and the asset is shared, two Agents could pursue the same target chain, and nothing in this document allocates territory. What the Atlas provides instead is a gating sequence — Operational GovOps alignment before commitment (A.2.2.8.1.1.1.1.2) — which surfaces duplicates in conversation rather than in contract.
description: Builders are reimbursed and given first-mover incentives, which is how the Atlas funds shared technical infrastructure that no single Agent could justify building alone.
